Author: Sharad Kumar Sharma
Bench: Sharad Kumar Sharma

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 No.1932 of 2023  With  IA/1/2023 (Compounding Application)

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. P.C. Petshali, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Mr. Yogesh Upadhyay, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Naveen Singh Bisht, learned counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3.
The parties are present in person.
They have been duly identified by their respective counsels.

This Court has interacted with the complainant, father of respondent no.3, who has made a statement that, owing to the subsequent development, because of the marriage, which has taken place between the applicant and respondent no.3, coupled with the fact, that out of the matrimony,
the applicant and respondent no.3 are having two children, he would not be having any grievance, as such, if the proceedings of SST No.56 of 2020, "State Vs. Prem Nandan" is quashed in terms of the compounding application.

Though all the offences, for which the summons has been issued i.e. the offence under Section 363,
366A, 376 of the IPC and Section 3(a)/4 of the POCSO Act, they may not be compoundable under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C., but this Court will have to carve out an exception owing to the circumstances of the instant case, for the reason being, that the facts, which have been brought on record in the compounding application, apart from the fact, that the factum of marriage is admitted to the parties, which stands fortified by the marriage registration certificate, as it has been placed on record.

The registration of the marriage finds reference in S.No.112 at SRO Office, Aonla,
District-Bareilly, showing that the marriage between the applicant and respondent no.3 has been registered, coupled with the fact, that out of the matrimony, they have got two children.
No fruitful purpose will be served to keep the proceedings pending.

In view of the fact, that the parties have married and the same is registered.
They have got two children, out of the matrimony, the complainant has got no objection.
As such, the compounding application would stand allowed.

As a consequence thereto, the proceedings of SST No.56 of 2020, "State Vs. Prem Nandan" as pending consideration before the Court of Special Judge/POCSO, Haldwani, District Nainital, would hereby stand quashed, in terms of the compounding application.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 18.10.2023
Sukhbant
